page: The Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is an x86_64 architecture virtual server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features 6 shared vCPUs mapped to 3 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU resources are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks reflect the shared CPU allocation of this instance. Single-core performance is generally weak, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1272.09 and a Geekbench single-core score of 796.0. Multi-core performance scales to average levels, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 6774.42. Memory bandwidth is mixed, offering an average read-only small block speed of 407.68 GB/sec but a weaker uncached write speed of 18.72 GB/sec. Computational workloads like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression score in the lower percentiles.

Given the shared CPU architecture and weaker single-core performance, this server is best suited for non-critical, budget-conscious workloads. It is appropriate for basic web serving, development environments, and lightweight multi-threaded applications that can utilize the 6 vCPUs without requiring sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The 320 GB NVMe SSD provides decent local storage capacity, but database operations and Redis SET operations remain in the lower performance tiers, indicating it is not designed for high-throughput transactional databases.
